subject: Re: Visibility Hub connector syndication & co-sell next steps
messages:
From: Kris Nolan <kris@observly.io>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Samantha Perez <sam.perez@cloudops-consulting.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Introducing Observly Visibility Hub connector for Redwood

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking a slot to chat with us at KubeCon — really enjoyed the runtime conversation. Observly has built a lightweight Visibility Hub that normalizes telemetry from OpenTelemetry, Datadog agents, and common metric sources, and we think a packaged connector for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments could drive meaningful co-sell motion with SRE customers.

High-level ask: would Redwood be open to a technical integration + joint GTM sprint that includes:
- a certified connector binary (lightweight sidecar) for Private/VPC installs
- a managed ingestion path for Hosted customers via Datadog/OTLP handoff
- a co-branded launch playbook and one joint customer pilot

I attached a short MOA that outlines responsibilities and a rough timeline. Technical lead (cc'd) is Samantha from CloudOps Consulting — they've helped us with a couple of marketplace listings.

Would love to schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive next week with your integrations engineering and partner ops. Proposed slots: Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks,
Kris
Kris Nolan
Head of Partnerships, Observly
attachments: observly-redwood-moa.pdf
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Kris Nolan <kris@observly.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Introducing Observly Visibility Hub connector for Redwood

Kris —

Appreciate the note and the MOA. This is in-scope for our integrations program. Quick answers up-front:
- Technical deep-dive: yes, please — Wed 08/18 10:00 PT works for me and I can bring our runtime integration lead (Ben) and partner GTM (Laura).
- Pilot ask: we prefer a single pilot with a clear success criteria matrix (latency overhead, ingestion reliability, security posture).

I reviewed the MOA and marked a couple of items for legal/partner ops to clarify (data ownership and support SLAs). Can we add a short SLO table and a security evidence checklist before the call? That will make the technical session more productive.

I'll schedule the call and include an agenda.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Partner Technical Manager, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Introductions from Observly — prep notes for Wed

Folks — quick internal prep before we accept the MOA and slot the eng deep-dive. My take:

Key technical checkpoints we should insist on before any pilot:
1) Connector footprint: memory/CPU at idle and during high-cardinality ingestion.
2) Auth flow: must support mutual TLS and integrate with our KMS for key rotation.
3) Configuration: must be declarative YAML that can be templated into our Private deploys.
4) Failure modes: how does it behave on network partitions and backpressure?

Commercial / ops asks:
- Need a clear support matrix: who triages first line, escalation to Observly vs Redwood.
- Revenue share / referral mechanics for co-sell leads.

I'm happy to own the tech checklist and run the sandbox eval if the lead engineers give access.

— Ben
Senior Integrations Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Kris Nolan <kris@observly.io>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Samantha Perez <sam.perez@cloudops-consulting.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Introductions from Observly — prep notes for Wed

Ben — thanks for the checklist. Quick responses inline:
- Footprint: connector is ~150MB resident, CPU idle ~40-60m, spikes depend on tail-cardinality. We'll share benchmarks (attached spec) and a small perf harness.
- Auth: we support mTLS and can add a KMS integration; will document key rotation and provisioning steps.
- Config: yes, YAML-first and templatable (we will attach the connector spec).
- Failure modes: connector queues and backpressures to disk with configurable retention; we will include circuit-breaker settings.

Attachments: visibility-hub-connector-spec.yaml (perf numbers and config knobs), perf-harness-sample.log (snippet), dd-partner-sla-draft.docx (commercial SLA for review).

We can confirm Wed 08/18 10:00 PT. Will bring two engineers and Samantha from CloudOps Consulting to help with install questions.

Kris
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Kris Nolan <kris@observly.io>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Visibility Hub connector syndication & co-sell next steps

Kris — thanks for the spec and SLA draft. A couple of commercial and GTM asks from my side:
- Co-sell lead flow: define how inbound leads are routed and a standard intake form (we can supply a HubSpot form template).
- Joint press/announcement: timeline depends on a pilot signed-off by both sides.
- Marketplace listing: what packaging do you need for the Datadog and Grafana marketplaces? We can share our template.

Action items agreed on the call:
1) Observly to share a short test harness + container image access (done).
2) Redwood to run a sandbox install and validate perf within 10 business days.
3) Legal to sync on the SLA redlines — Laura will loop in Partner Ops.

I'll track the intake form and draft the co-sell intake flow. Meeting notes and recording in the related Drive link.

— Laura
Head of Partner GTM, Redwood Inference
attachments referenced: hubspot-form-template.xlsx
From: Samantha Perez <sam.perez@cloudops-consulting.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, Kris Nolan <kris@observly.io>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Observly sandbox access + next steps

Looping in a short checklist from CloudOps Consulting as we hand off the sandbox:
- Provide container registry credentials (read-only)
- Share Helm charts / kustomize overlay for Private installations
- Provide sample OTLP payloads and a Datadog agent config for end-to-end validation
- Access window: 48 hours of elevated support starting Wed 08/25; CloudOps will be on-call for first installs

I've attached a short runbook and will open a Jira ticket with the tasks and owners. If Redwood can confirm the registry creds and a PoC cluster by EOD Tue 08/24 we'll hit the 10-day sandbox validation SLA.

Regards,
Sam Perez
CloudOps Consulting (on behalf of Observly)
attachments: cloudops-sandbox-runbook.pdf
